## Motivation

FlashInfer autotune persistence never pays off for ops that profile under a non-default measurement policy. The trtllm-gen FP4 MoE (`flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`) profiles with cold L2, and the v1 JSON files written by `save_configs` record no per-entry policy. So while tuning, `AutoTuner.search_cache` skips every file entry for that op, and every boot re-profiles it from scratch, even when the file holds the exact keys. On a B300 Kimi-K3 deployment that is about 4 minutes of startup per pod, with a fully seeded, matching cache on disk.

FlashInfer's `autotune_v2` managed store is the fix path. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5495 records each entry's profiling policy in that store, so a cold-L2 winner is reused on the next boot. The v1 file path stays gated by design. This PR moves sglang onto `autotune_v2` so it picks that up.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/flashinfer_autotune.py`
- **One store per rank, attached once per process** (`attach_flashinfer_autotune_store`).
  - `autotune_v2` attaches its store for the whole process, and the last attach wins. Serving then reads tuned winners from that store's partition.
  - So the target, extend, draft and PCIe-IPC tuning passes all have to tune into a single store that is attached before the first of them runs.
  - Root: `$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/flashinfer/autotune/managed/<key>/rank_tp{}_pp{}_dp{}`. FlashInfer adds its own environment namespace below it (library versions, GPU).
- **Cross-rank agreement gate rebuilt over the store** (`_agree_on_autotune_store`). Same contract as before: a store hit skips a profile, so ranks that would hit differently desync the per-profile timing all-reduce.
  - Each rank all-gathers a digest of its entries plus its FlashInfer environment. The environment picks which namespace a rank reads, so equal stores alone do not mean equal hits.
  - If the digests diverge, every rank wipes its own store, then votes again on whether the wipe worked. If any rank still has entries, every rank tunes in memory only, so the group never splits.
  - The gate runs before the store is attached, because attaching loads the store into memory.
  - Every branch is decided on gathered values, so all ranks take the same one.
- **TP groups: exclusive `flock` on each rank's store, held for the process lifetime.**
  - FlashInfer reads keys missing from its attach-time snapshot from disk on first lookup. Without the lock, a second server on the same host publishing into the same root mid-tuning could split a TP group on a hit.
  - A single rank (TP=1) takes no lock and skips the gate. It has no group to split, and FlashInfer publishes each entry atomically, so co-located TP=1 servers of one model share one store.
  - If any rank can't lock its store, every rank tunes in memory only. The failing rank logs why (held by another process, root not creatable, or `flock` unsupported).
- `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE=0` now tunes into a fresh timestamped store instead of a timestamped JSON file (docs updated).
- The manual `load_configs` / `save_configs` dance around `autotune(True)` is gone. v2 never touches `_file_configs`, so the draft worker can no longer drop the target's loaded tactics.

`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/base_runner.py`
- `warmup()` attaches the store **before** `_pre_initialize_pcie_ipc_workspace()`.
- PCIe-IPC tunes through `AutoTuner.choose_one` in its `prepare()`. Winners tuned before the attach land in the plain in-memory cache, which serving stops reading once a store is attached.

## Dependency

The startup win needs a FlashInfer release that contains flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5495 (open and approved as of this PR). On the pinned `flashinfer_python==0.7.0.post1` this change is behavior-neutral for cold-L2 ops: they re-tune every boot, exactly as today. Default-policy ops reuse store entries just as they reused v1 file entries.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This changes where tuned tactics are persisted and when they are reused, not tactic selection.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, 1x B300 (sm103). Two boots per row against the same cache dir. The time is the first autotune round (`Running FlashInfer autotune` → `FlashInfer autotune completed`).

| sglang | flashinfer | boot 1 | boot 2 | boot 2 profiled `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 0.7.0.post1 | 115 s | 94 s | yes |
| **this PR** | **0.7.0.post1 + #5495** | 104 s | **2 s** | **no** |
| `main` (v1 files) | 0.7.0.post1 + #5495 | 105 s | 96 s | yes |

Only the sglang side differs between the last two rows.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit.
- [x] Unit tests: `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py`, 29 passed on B300, CUDA-only tests included, against both stock 0.7.0.post1 and 0.7.0.post1 + #5495. Each guard was mutation-checked, and each mutant fails its intended test:
  - once-per-process attach, and the attach alone rooting the process store
  - TP groups hold the lock for the process lifetime, while single ranks share a store another server holds
  - gate before load, and attach before PCIe-IPC
  - wipe on divergence, plus the re-vote after a failed wipe
  - unanimous fallback when a rank is unlocked
  - environment compared, and digest over entry content
  - root per rank and per dtype, and the reuse-off branch
- [x] TP=2 end-to-end (gpt-oss-20b, 2x B300, 0.7.0.post1 + #5495), four boots against one cache dir:

  | boot | setup | first autotune round | tuned? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | cold | 127 s | yes |
  | 2 | warm | 2 s | no |
  | 3 | one entry deleted from rank 1's store only | 114 s | yes, after `per-rank stores disagree, discarding them`; no hang |
  | 4 | warm | 2 s | no |

  After boot 1, rank 0's and rank 1's 20 entries were byte-identical. Boot 3's wipe-and-retune restored 20/20 on both ranks.

Thanks @Kangyan-Zhou for taking the initiative to integrate `autotune_v2` into SGLang, and for including the partial-cache restart test and target/draft store-lifetime handling! I'm working on the related [vLLM migration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55671), and would like to help get this landed.

We can help with the FlashInfer cache-contract review, additional TP+EP cold/warm-start and model-accuracy validation, and coordination around [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5495](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5495) and the subsequent release/pin. We have a rank-cache hang reproducer from the vLLM work that should also help inform the validation here.

One case worth checking together is legitimate rank-specific EP entries: [#40420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40420) reports that whole-cache equality can discard valid per-rank caches on every restart. The managed-store digest here appears to retain that conservative behavior. We should verify warm reuse for such a configuration while keeping your partial-cache safety guarantee; matching environment metadata alone would not establish matching per-op profiling participation. I haven't run this SGLang branch yet, so this is a review/validation target, not a reproduced failure on this PR.

I also checked the main PR-test gate: it currently stops because the PR is a draft, before the GPU tests run. The cold-L2 startup improvement remains a separate dependency on the FlashInfer fix, as your description notes.

What would help you most first: an independent EP/lifecycle review and validation, or help working through the FlashInfer dependency? Happy to coordinate the split with you.

> @Kangyan-Zhou, [[FlashInfer #5705](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5705)]([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5705](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5705)) shipped in 0.7.1 and preserves per-entry replay/L2 profiling policy through the existing v1 save/load path. SGLang main now pins 0.7.1, so the original cold-L2 cache-reuse fix no longer requires migrating to v2.
> 
> Could you confirm this with the original reproduction configuration on stock FlashInfer 0.7.1: one cold startup with a fresh cache, followed by a warm restart against the same cache, verifying that the warm run skips profiling the affected operation? If confirmed, I suggest closing this PR as no longer needed for its original motivation and considering the managed-v2 migration separately.
> 
> cc @Fridge003

Thanks, I'll close the PR for now and report if the issue still persists

One validation point: switching to `autotune_v2` can change tactic selection as well as persistence. In FlashInfer `0.7.0.post1`, v2 enables `race_default`, adding `(runners[0], tactic=-1)` to the candidate list when absent https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.0.post1/flashinfer/autotuner/autotuner.py#L2367-L2374. That can change the winning tactic, so the description’s assertion that tactic selection is unchanged is too strong.

Could you update the Accuracy Tests section and report a focused output-correctness smoke test on the existing gpt-oss/B300 setup, covering both cold tuning and warm-cache restart, including CUDA Graph replay if enabled? A focused check on that setup would be sufficient for this PR’s persistence scope.

Thanks @Kangyan-Zhou for taking the initiative to integrate `autotune_v2` into SGLang, and for including the partial-cache restart test and target/draft store-lifetime handling! I'm working on the related [vLLM migration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55671), and would like to help get this landed.

We can help with the FlashInfer cache-contract review, additional TP+EP cold/warm-start and model-accuracy validation, and coordination around [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5495](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5495) and the subsequent release/pin. We have a rank-cache hang reproducer from the vLLM work that should also help inform the validation here.

One case worth checking together is legitimate rank-specific EP entries: [#40420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40420) reports that whole-cache equality can discard valid per-rank caches on every restart. The managed-store digest here appears to retain that conservative behavior. We should verify warm reuse for such a configuration while keeping your partial-cache safety guarantee; matching environment metadata alone would not establish matching per-op profiling participation. I haven't run this SGLang branch yet, so this is a review/validation target, not a reproduced failure on this PR.

I also checked the main PR-test gate: it currently stops because the PR is a draft, before the GPU tests run. The cold-L2 startup improvement remains a separate dependency on the FlashInfer fix, as your description notes.

What would help you most first: an independent EP/lifecycle review and validation, or help working through the FlashInfer dependency? Happy to coordinate the split with you.

> @Kangyan-Zhou, [[FlashInfer #5705](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5705)]([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5705](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5705)) shipped in 0.7.1 and preserves per-entry replay/L2 profiling policy through the existing v1 save/load path. SGLang main now pins 0.7.1, so the original cold-L2 cache-reuse fix no longer requires migrating to v2.
> 
> Could you confirm this with the original reproduction configuration on stock FlashInfer 0.7.1: one cold startup with a fresh cache, followed by a warm restart against the same cache, verifying that the warm run skips profiling the affected operation? If confirmed, I suggest closing this PR as no longer needed for its original motivation and considering the managed-v2 migration separately.
> 
> cc @Fridge003

Thanks, I'll close the PR for now and report if the issue still persists
